writeup.headline: GitLab rates Hold: solid growth, net cash and strong momentum offset by high absolute valuation and GAAP losses.
writeup.thesis: GitLab scores 60, a Hold, 5 points below the Buy band. Growth is a strength, with TTM revenue growth of 23.0% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 21.3% year on year, though growth slowed by 1.8 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 thanks to net cash and no debt, and the trend score of 84 reflects the price at its 52-week high and shares 155.5 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Holding the rating back are valuation (26), with P/S of 9.3x and P/FCF of 45.8x high in absolute terms and an FCF yield 2.8 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, even though the stock is cheap against its own history on P/S (cheaper than at 40 of the last 55 month-ends). Quality is middling at 49: an 85.8% gross margin and 20.2% FCF margin sit against a -8.6% operating margin and stock-based compensation of 21.8% of revenue.
key_risks: Further growth deceleration after growth slowed by 1.8 pp from the previous quarter
GAAP operating losses and stock-based compensation at 21.8% of revenue, with diluted share count up 1.7% year on year
High absolute multiples (9.3x sales, 45.8x FCF) leave little room for disappointment
After a sharp run (price 71.2% above its 200-day average), momentum could reverse
Competitive pressure in AI-driven developer platforms; next results expected 2026-12-01
what_would_change: A 5-point score gain would reach Buy, for example from re-accelerating revenue growth or a lower valuation multiple lifting the valuation score
Progress toward GAAP operating profit or lower stock-based compensation would raise the quality score
A drop of 16 points would be needed for Sell, such as a sharp reversal in trend combined with weaker growth or negative news on guidance
